about: Bonvoyage protocol v1 test vectors. All binary values are base64url without padding. See README.md.

base64url.note: AR decodes to the same byte as AQ, and AQJ to the same bytes as AQI, but with non-zero unused bits.

hosts.note: localhost (with a port) is only a host in a client's development mode, which is off by default.

must_accept.note: Each opens and passes steps 1 to 6 of receiving at time `now`.

may_reject.note: The spec lets a receiver accept or reject these (section 1.2). Either is conformant.

contact_checks.note: The recipient has ONE contact: created from `cards.valid` at time `contact.issued`, not yet paired. Handle the steps in order at time `now`. `pinned_after` is the signing key pinned to the contact after that step, or null.

steps.why: a valid message from a stranger: the pairing secret matches no contact
right pairing secret, but not a ticket: it must not pair, or a card thief could pair without anything printing
right pairing secret, but the ticket is invalid: it must not pair either
right pairing secret and a valid ticket: the sender is paired and pinned
same signing key and id as the previous message: a repeat
right pairing secret and a valid ticket, but the contact is pinned to another key: the card reached someone else
the pinned sender: the pairing secret is no longer looked at
authentic, but an unknown message type is dropped without printing
created more than 600 seconds before the contact's card was issued
created exactly 600 seconds before the card was issued: still accepted

expired_card.note: A fresh, unpaired copy of the same contact, handled at time `now`, which is after the card expired.

text_cleaning.note: C1 controls, DEL, carriage return, paragraph separator, BOM, a format character outside the basic plane
the joiners U+200D and U+200C are kept

relay_response.note: A collect response a client must handle: it looks at the first 20 entries only, and of those skips every one without a valid relay message id.
